title: Concentration Plus Drift: How Provider Monoculture Turns a Silent Model Update into a Correlated Regression

original_idea.body:
# Concentration Plus Drift: How Provider Monoculture Turns a Silent Model Update into a Correlated Regression

**Problem:** Failure mode A: silent model updates / behavioral drift breaking downstream systems. Failure mode B: provider concentration (homogeneity-driven dependence on few models). When many systems depend on the same model, one update is a correlated, simultaneous regression across all of them.

**Direction:** Using two snapshots/versions of available open models (or two checkpoints), build a small suite of downstream 'contracts' (format, refusal boundary, factual answers). Measure how many contracts break per version change, and simulate fleet impact: if N systems share the model, one update breaks correlated subsets. Produce a 'blast radius of an update' estimate tied to concentration.

**Why it matters:** The International AI Safety Report highlights cascading failures from shared-provider dependence. A concrete, measured demonstration of correlated regression risk from a single update is a tangible systemic-risk contribution feasible with open checkpoints.

**Relevant context:** International AI Safety Report 2026 cascading/concentration risk; Artificial Hivemind homogeneity; behavioral-drift literature.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Correlated-regression blast-radius is a plausible systemic-risk chain but reliability-flavored with a gap to catastrophic AI risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a contract suite over two checkpoints is guided work novices can do with mentorship.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused 'blast radius' deliverable; contract-suite design plus fleet-simulation adds some scope.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open checkpoints, no lab access; systemic-risk measurement is independent-friendly.

novelty.reasoning: Behavioral drift studied; the concentration-blast-radius framing may be partially open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Drift studied; blast-radius-tied-to-concentration framing may be open.
